chapter_name: Chapter 15: Creative Writing (Story and Narrative Writing)
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will craft compelling short stories by understanding narrative arcs, developing character perspectives, and applying the 'Show, Don't Tell' technique.]
warm_up_hook: 🎬 Every great movie, book, and video game starts as a story on a piece of paper. Today, you are the director, the actor, and the set designer. It's time to build a world from scratch! 🌍

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Every story needs a beginning (Introduction/Setting the scene), a middle (Rising Action and Climax—the most exciting part where the problem peaks), and an end (Resolution—how the problem is solved). Without conflict or a problem, a story is just a boring report.
examples_or_templates: Conflict: The hero wants something, but an obstacle stands in their way.
Climax: The moment the hero finally faces the obstacle head-on.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Instead of simply stating an emotion or fact, describe the physical actions or environment that prove it. This makes the reader figure it out themselves, which is much more engaging.
examples_or_templates: Showing: 'John bit his fingernails, his knee bouncing rapidly up and down beneath the desk.'

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Characters talking (dialogue) moves the story forward and shows personality. Always start a new paragraph when a different character speaks. Use varied speech tags (whispered, shouted, muttered) instead of just 'said'.
examples_or_templates: Example: 'I can't believe you did that,' she whispered, refusing to meet his eyes.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which part of the story arc contains the highest tension and the main turning point?
❓ Which sentence is the best example of 'Show, Don't Tell' for the emotion of anger?
options: He was extremely angry at his brother.
His face turned red and he slammed his fists onto the table.
He felt a deep sense of rage.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: His face turned red and he slammed his fists onto the table.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this 'Telling' sentence into 'Showing': 'The weather was freezing.'
subjective_practice.hint: Describe breath turning to fog, shivering, or ice forming on windows.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a three-line dialogue between a student and a teacher where the student is trying to hide that they lost their homework.
subjective_practice.hint: Use nervous actions and speech tags like 'stammered' or 'mumbled' instead of just 'said'.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🚪 The Mysterious Door
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write a 150-word story that begins with this exact sentence: 'The old wooden door at the end of the hallway had never been unlocked, until today.' Make sure your story has a clear conflict and a climax!

chapter_summary: ⭐ A satisfying story needs a clear arc: Introduction, Conflict, Climax, and Resolution.
⭐ 'Show, Don't Tell' immerses the reader by describing actions and sensory details rather than stating facts.
⭐ Good dialogue reveals character personality and breaks up long blocks of text to improve pacing.
